title: Hotel101 Global Tops Off Hotel101-Niseko in Hokkaido, Japan on Track for December 2026 Opening
summary: HOTEL101-NISEKO WITH ITS 1.17 HECTARE PRIME SITE AND 482 ROOMS IS EXPECTED TO BE ONE OF THE LARGEST HOTELS IN THE HEART OF HIRAFU, NISEKO, HOKKAIDO, JAPAN BY ROOM COUNT, LOCATED ABOUT 2 MINUTES BY SHUTTLE TO THE SKI LIFTS HOTEL101-NISEKO’S TOPPING OFF CEREMONY CONDUCTED TODAY HIGHLIGHTS THE
body_text: Hotel101 Global Tops Off Hotel101-Niseko in Hokkaido, Japan on Track for December 2026 Opening December 5, 2025 PDF Version Picture 1 DoubleDragon Corporation Founders Edgar “Injap” Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong at the Topping Off Ceremony of Hotel101-Niseko held today December 5, 2025 Picture 2 DoubleDragon Corporation Founders Edgar “Injap” Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong with Hotel101 Global CEO Hannah Yulo-Luccini at topmost floor of Hotel101-Niseko project site Picture 2 Aerial Photo of 482-room Hotel101-Niseko in the heart of Hirafu, Niseko, Hokkaido Japan HOTEL101-NISEKO WITH ITS 1.17 HECTARE PRIME SITE AND 482 ROOMS IS EXPECTED TO BE ONE OF THE LARGEST HOTELS IN THE HEART OF HIRAFU, NISEKO, HOKKAIDO, JAPAN BY ROOM COUNT, LOCATED ABOUT 2 MINUTES BY SHUTTLE TO THE SKI LIFTS HOTEL101-NISEKO’S TOPPING OFF CEREMONY CONDUCTED TODAY HIGHLIGHTS THE EXPECTED COMPLETION OF THE WHOLE BUILDING STRUCTURE, TO BE FOLLOWED BY THE FULL SWING INTERIOR FINISHING WORKS IN TIME FOR THE EXPECTED HOTEL OPENING IN DECEMBER 2026. HOTEL101-NISEKO’S COMPLETION PROGRESS IS ON SCHEDULE DoubleDragon Corporation Founders Edgar “Injap” Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong at the Topping Off Ceremony of Hotel101-Niseko held today December 5, 2025 DoubleDragon Corporation Founders Edgar “Injap” Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong at the Topping Off Ceremony of Hotel101-Niseko held today December 5, 2025 DoubleDragon Corporation Founders Edgar “Injap” Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong with Hotel101 Global CEO Hannah Yulo-Luccini at topmost floor of Hotel101-Niseko project site DoubleDragon Corporation Founders Edgar “Injap” Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong with Hotel101 Global CEO Hannah Yulo-Luccini at topmost floor of Hotel101-Niseko project site SINGAPORE, Dec. 05, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hotel101 Global Holdings Corp. (NASDAQ Ticker: HBNB) (“Hotel101” or “Hotel101 Global”), a leading asset-light, prop-tech hospitality platform pioneering a global standardized “condotel” business model listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange and a subsidiary of Philippine-listed DoubleDragon Corporation (PSE Ticker: DD), tops off 482-room Hotel101-Niseko, which is set to be [one of] the largest hotel in Hirafu by room count. Expected to open in December 2026, the property is expected to welcome guests in time for the 2026–2027 winter season in one of the world’s most celebrated ski destinations. More than just a hotel, Hotel101-Niseko introduces an innovative “condotel” model that combines exceptional value with world-class amenities and unmistakable Filipino warmth. Every one of the 482 identically designed, efficiently laid-out rooms is expected to offer practical comfort tailored to the needs of modern travelers—whether families, couples, or groups of friends chasing powder in Niseko. In addition, guests can expect to look forward to unparalleled amenities for the value segment such as: All-day dining restaurant Dedicated meeting spaces and business center Indoor swimming pool and hot mineral onsen bath Sauna and wellness facilities 24-hour front desk and concierge Ski lockers and ski-in/ski-out convenience On-site convenience store Complimentary shuttle service to Grand Hirafu lifts Located in the vibrant heart of Hirafu, Hotel101-Niseko is expected to place visitors steps away from Niseko’s legendary powder snow, renowned restaurants, and lively après-ski scene, while offering a welcoming sanctuary that reflects the heartfelt hospitality the Philippines is famous for worldwide. Niseko, a mountain village that now attracts more than two million international visitors annually from over thirty countries, continues to solidify its reputation as Asia’s premier alpine destination. With the rise of Hotel101-Niseko, a bold new landmark joins this global playground—proof that Filipino innovation and hospitality have earned their place among the very best in the world. Construction remains on schedule, with the property counting down to its expected grand opening in time for the 2026 winter season. Aerial Photo of 482-room Hotel101-Niseko in the heart of Hirafu, Niseko, Hokkaido Japan Aerial Photo of 482-room Hotel101-Niseko in the heart of Hirafu, Niseko, Hokkaido, Japan About Hotel101 Global Listed on Nasdaq (HBNB) with a market capitalization of approximately US$1.5 billion as of December 4, 2025, Hotel101 is an asset-light, prop-tech hospitality platform pioneering a global standardized “condotel” business model. Hotel101 aims to disrupt the global hotel and hospitality sector through its unique tech-enabled business model that positions it to generate revenues twice: first from the advance sale of individual hotel units during the construction phase; and second, from long-term recurring revenue derived from day-to-day hotel operations. Hotel101 and its affiliates have nine Hotel101-branded properties in the Philippines in various stages of operations and development, as well as three projects under development overseas in Hokkaido (Japan), Madrid (Spain), and Los Angeles (United States). In May 2025, Hotel101 signed an agreement with Saudi Arabia’s Horizon Group to, subject to additional contract, establish a joint venture for the development of up to 10 hotels in Saudi Arabia. In November 2025, Hotel101 signed an agreement for the development of a Hotel101 project in Milan, Italy, subject to customary national, regional and municipal regulatory approvals. Hotel101 aspires to operate 1 million rooms across 100 countries worldwide, with an initial 25 identified priority countries for the medium term. Hotel101 is a subsidiary of Philippine-listed DoubleDragon Corporation (PSE Ticker: DD). title: Payroll Assistant: Complete Career Guide (2026)
summary: Learn everything you need to know about payroll assistant career paths, including salary ranges and step-by-step guidance to break into this stable, growing field.
body_text: With about 130,000 payroll assistants employed in the U.S. earning a median salary of $52,480 per year, this essential role keeps America’s workforce paid accurately and on time. Whether you’re switching careers or just starting out, payroll offers something rare: job security, competitive pay, and advancement opportunities that don't require years of schooling. This guide covers everything you need to know about breaking into the field, from salary expectations to the skills that matter most. TL;DR: Payroll assistant career guide What payroll assistants do : Process employee wages, maintain payroll records, handle tax compliance, and support employees with payroll questions—ensuring accurate, timely paychecks every pay period. Salary potential : The national average salary is $52,480 annually, which ranges from $43,468 (entry-level) to $76,093+ (senior roles). Your location, industry, and experience significantly impact earnings. Education needed : A high school diploma is usually required. A college degree can be helpful, but it isn’t mandatory. Professional certifications like FPC and CPP can boost career prospects and advancement opportunities. Essential skills : Employers often look for strong math abilities, attention to detail, computer proficiency, and excellent communication skills. Comfort with systematic processes and ability to handle confidential information are also crucial. Career growth : The typical advancement path is from assistant to specialist to manager, which often takes 2-3 years between levels. Remote work is increasingly common, and going freelance is an option. To get started : Focus on developing transferable skills through administrative or customer service roles, consider getting certified, and target smaller companies for comprehensive training and faster advancement. {{banner-cta}} What is a payroll assistant? A payroll assistant handles the behind-the-scenes work that keeps paychecks flowing to your team: processing employee wages, maintaining payroll records, and ensuring compliance with tax regulations. You’ll find them working under different titles—payroll clerk, payroll coordinator, or similar. But their core job stays the same: keeping payroll accurate, compliant, and stress-free for everyone, from neighborhood coffee shops to massive corporations. What does a payroll assistant do? Daily duties and responsibilities The day-to-day work of a payroll assistant revolves around one mission: getting your team paid correctly and on time. A typical day in the life of a payroll assistant might include tasks like: Timekeeping and hour verification : This includes collecting and verifying employee timesheets from punch cards, digital time clocks, or time tracking apps like Homebase , double-checking that recorded hours match reality and ensuring approved time off gets properly recorded in the payroll system. Payroll processing : Payroll assistants enter verified hours into payroll software , calculate regular pay and overtime, and process bonuses and commissions from the payroll bank account , whether for nonprofit payroll or other industries. Then they handle payment distribution through direct deposits , paper checks, or payroll cards while double-checking calculations for accuracy to ensure the business account balance is maintained. Employee data management : As a payroll assistant, you’re expected to keep employee information current by updating systems when someone gets a raise, changes tax withholding or direct deposit info ; set up profiles for new hires, and process final paychecks when employees leave. Tax and compliance : This includes calculating and withholding federal, state , and local taxes from each paycheck while staying current with changing regulations, preparing tax deposits, and assisting with quarterly reporting. Employee support : Payroll assistants serve as the first point of contact for payroll questions. You may be asked to explain deductions and ordinary income , troubleshoot direct deposit issues, find advice numbers , walk people through their payroll statements , and resolve discrepancies . Payroll assistant salary and compensation Let’s talk money. What can you actually expect to earn as a payroll assistant? The short answer: it depends on where you work, who you work for, and how much experience you bring to the table. National salary averages According to current Glassdoor data , payroll assistants earn an average of $52,480 per year, which works out to about $25 per hour. Here’s how salaries break down: The bottom 25% typically earn $43,468 annually, usually in entry-level positions. The median salary range is around $52,480 annually. Payroll assistants in this category typically have mid-level experience. Experienced payroll professionals tend to make $63,920 annually, making them the top 25% earners. The top 10% earners are typically payroll assistants working in senior roles or premium markets whose salaries are around $76,093 annually. What affects your payroll assistant salary Several factors can push your salary higher or lower than the national average: Location makes a big difference . Cities like San Francisco, New York, and Seattle typically pay 20-30% above average, while smaller towns might offer 10-15% less. Industry matters too . Healthcare, finance, and tech companies often pay premium wages for payroll expertise. Company size impacts compensation . Larger organizations usually offer higher salaries and more comprehensive benefits for more complex payroll needs. Your experience level is the biggest factor . Entry-level roles focus on basic tasks while experienced assistants handle complex compliance and training responsibilities. Benefits and total compensation Base salary is just part of the story. Most payroll assistant positions come with benefit packages that add real value—health insurance, retirement plans with company matching, paid time off, and professional development opportunities. Some companies provide payroll-specific perks like certification reimbursement or conference attendance, which can accelerate your career growth and earning potential. Essential skills for payroll assistant success Some people are naturally suited for payroll work, while others can develop the necessary skills with practice. Either way, you’ll need some key skills and traits to succeed in payroll roles. Technical skills you need As expected, you’ll need strong math skills and computer proficiency. You also need to be comfortable with: Mathematical calculations, including percentages and basic algebra Computer systems and software applications Payroll concepts like tax calculations and overtime rules (these come with training) Having a logical mind that enjoys systematic processes helps you learn faster. Soft skills that matter These interpersonal and work style skills determine how well you handle the human side of payroll: Attention to detail : Small mistakes create big paycheck problems, so accuracy is non-negotiable. Confidentiality and discretion : You’ll handle sensitive salary and personal information. Time management : Payroll deadlines are firm, which means you’ll need excellent organization skills. Communication skills : You need to be able to explain complex payroll deductions and handle employee concerns. Problem-solving : Discrepancies can come up regularly, and will need quick resolution. Personality traits that fit the role Certain personality characteristics align well with payroll work: Detail-oriented perfectionists tend to thrive in environments where accuracy matters more than speed, while people who like routine and structure can appreciate payroll’s predictable cycles and systematic processes. Those with calm personalities can handle deadline pressure and employee concerns without easily getting stressed. Trustworthy individuals naturally protect confidential information and maintain ethical standards, which is crucial in payroll work. For those who are service-oriented, this job can provide satisfaction in helping employees understand their pay and resolving their concerns. Patient communicators can excel in this role as they can explain payroll policies repeatedly without getting frustrated. ‍ Organized thinkers can make great payroll assistants too, as they can keep track of multiple deadlines and requirements without dropping the ball. Software skills worth developing Mastering these technologies will make you more effective and marketable: Microsoft Excel : You’ll need to understand and know how to use formulas, perform data manipulation, and generate reports for payroll analysis. Email and calendar management : This includes coordinating deadlines and employee communication. PDF tools : You’ll use these to create and edit documents for secure payroll reporting. Cloud storage platforms : These are essential for document management and collaboration. Adaptability with new software is also important, as different companies use different systems and regularly update technology. Since many systems have a mobile payroll app , you'll want to stay familiar with different hardware options too. How to become a payroll assistant: Step-by-step guide Ready to start your payroll career? Here’s a roadmap you can follow from where you are now to landing your first payroll assistant position. Step 1: Meet minimum qualifications Good news: you don’t need a four-year degree to start a payroll career. Ensure you have the basics: a high school diploma or General Education Development GED can get you in the door at most companies. Some employers may prefer additional education, but they will also train the right candidate regardless of formal background. While usually not required, associate degrees in business or accounting and bachelor’s degrees in finance or business management can give you an advantage and potentially fast-track you to higher-level positions. Step 2: Gain relevant experience (if no payroll background) Build transferable skills through administrative positions involving data entry and detail work, bookkeeping or accounting roles to understand financial processes, customer service jobs that develop communication skills, or volunteer work with nonprofits to gain hands-on experience. Step 3: Consider certification Professional certifications are optional, but can demonstrate commitment and expertise that employers value. The Fundamental Payroll Certification (FPC) from the American Payroll Association is perfect for beginners because it requires no prior experience and validates your understanding of basic payroll concepts through an exam covering processing fundamentals and compliance. The Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) requires three years of payroll experience and advanced education, making it the next step for career advancement and access to senior positions with higher compensation. Step 4: Tailor your resume and apply strategically Craft a resume highlighting attention to detail, mathematical ability, and technology comfort while emphasizing any experience with numbers, confidential information, or deadline pressure. Target smaller companies that provide comprehensive training and faster advancement opportunities. Step 5: Ace the interview Prepare for common payroll interview questions by developing specific examples that demonstrate your accuracy, confidentiality experience, ability to work under pressure, problem-solving skills, and customer service approach. These are the qualities employers value most in payroll candidates. Step 6: Excel in your first role Learn company systems thoroughly by asking questions rather than guessing, build positive relationships across departments, stay current with tax changes through professional resources, and volunteer for additional responsibilities that demonstrate your growth potential and commitment. {{banner-cta}} Career progression and advancement opportunities Unlike some careers where growth opportunities are limited, payroll offers multiple clear advancement paths for professionals willing to develop their expertise. The typical career ladder The payroll profession follows a predictable advancement structure: Entry level : Payroll assistant positions focus on basic processing and administrative tasks while you learn systems and procedures. Mid-level : After 2-3 years, advance to payroll specialist or senior payroll assistant roles handling complex calculations, compliance tasks, and training newer employees. Senior level : Payroll analyst positions involve system management, advanced compliance oversight, and project leadership, typically requiring 5+ years of experience. Management : Payroll supervisor or manager roles involve overseeing teams, coordinating with senior leadership, and making strategic decisions. Leadership : Payroll director positions focus on policy development, enterprise-wide compliance, and business strategy contribution. Adjacent career opportunities Payroll experience provides excellent preparation for related careers: Human Resources : Your compensation and employee data knowledge transfers well to HR roles. Accounting : Payroll assistants have a strong understanding of financial processes, so accounting roles can be a great adjacent career. Finance : The business operations knowledge from your payroll position can make your transition into a finance role easier. Consulting : As you’ve gained more experience, transitioning into a consulting role where you serve multiple clients independently can be a good career move. Payroll virtual assistant: Remote and freelance opportunities Payroll professionals now have more career flexibility than ever, with remote work and freelance opportunities becoming increasingly common. Remote payroll assistant opportunities Many companies now offer fully remote payroll positions since cloud-based software allows payroll assistants to complete most tasks from anywhere. These work-from-home opportunities include: Full-time positions with single employers Part-time arrangements for work-life balance Hybrid schedules combining office and home work Temporary contracts for specific projects Freelance and virtual assistant payroll work Experienced payroll professionals can build independent contractor practices and serve multiple small business clients who need payroll expertise but can't justify full-time staff. This typically involves managing 5-15 clients and offers higher earning potential plus schedule flexibility for those with strong client management skills. Many virtual assistants expand services to include bookkeeping, tax preparation, and other financial services, creating comprehensive business support practices. Payroll assistant vs. related roles Understanding how payroll assistant positions compare to similar roles helps clarify what to expect and where your career might lead. Payroll Assistant vs. Payroll Clerk Payroll clerks handle basic data entry and check payroll generation under close supervision, while payroll assistants take on broader responsibilities like employee support, problem resolution, and complex processing tasks. Smaller companies often use these titles interchangeably. Payroll Assistant vs. Payroll Specialist Payroll specialists manage comprehensive operations for larger organizations, handling complex tax compliance, advanced reporting, and system oversight while serving as subject matter experts. This represents a natural advancement path as you develop specialized knowledge. Payroll Assistant vs. Payroll Coordinator Payroll coordinators typically oversee processes and coordinate between departments, often supervising assistant-level staff while handling more strategic planning and interdepartmental communication. Payroll Assistant vs. HR Assistant While both provide administrative support, HR assistants focus on broader functions like recruitment and employee relations, while payroll assistants specialize specifically in compensation processing and compliance. Some smaller companies combine these roles. Tools and software payroll assistants use Payroll processing relies heavily on software systems that handle calculations, tax compliance, and reporting. You’ll likely encounter several different platforms throughout your career. Major payroll platforms Here are the systems you’ll most commonly work with: ADP Workforce Now : Dominates enterprise payroll with comprehensive HR functionality for medium to large businesses. Paychex : Serves small to mid-size businesses with user-friendly interfaces and strong customer support. QuickBooks Payroll : Integrates seamlessly with QuickBooks accounting, making it the go-to choice for small businesses. Gusto : Popular among small businesses for intuitive design and comprehensive features including benefits administration. Workday : Handles complex enterprise needs for large corporations requiring advanced reporting. UltraI payroll : Provides mid-market solutions with robust human capital management features. For small businesses with hourly teams, Homebase offers an integrated solution that combines scheduling , time tracking , and full-service payroll processing designed specifically for hourly workers. Every company uses different systems, and employers provide training on their chosen platforms. Focus on developing strong foundational payroll knowledge that transfers across different software systems. Timekeeping and scheduling software Modern payroll processing depends on integration between time tracking and payroll systems to ensure accurate data and reduce manual entry errors. Enterprise solutions like Kronos/UKG and ADP Time & Attendance provide seamless integration for large organizations with complex scheduling needs. Small business platforms including TSheets/QuickBooks Time and Homebase offer direct integration with their respective payroll systems. Standalone scheduling tools like When I Work and Deputy export data to various payroll platforms, though this requires more manual coordination. Direct data flow from time tracking to payroll eliminates manual entry errors and saves hours of administrative work each pay period. Integrated systems also provide better compliance tracking for break requirements and overtime calculations. Homebase’s fully integrated approach combines scheduling, time tracking, and payroll in one platform, allowing payroll assistants to process accurate payroll in minutes rather than hours. FAQ: Payroll assistant career What does a payroll assistant do? A payroll assistant ensures employees get paid accurately and on time by processing wages, maintaining records, calculating tax withholdings, and handling payroll-related questions. Daily work includes verifying timesheets, entering data into payroll systems, preparing paychecks, and helping employees understand their pay. What is an example of a payroll assistant job description? A typical payroll assistant job posting might read: We’re looking for a detail-oriented payroll assistant to process bi-weekly payroll for our 150-person team. You’ll verify timesheets, calculate wages and deductions, maintain employee records, and ensure compliance with tax regulations. Perfect for someone with strong math skills, attention to detail, and interest in learning payroll software. Is payroll a high-paying job? Payroll offers competitive compensation with good growth potential. According to current Glassdoor data, payroll assistants earn an average of $52,480 per year. Entry-level positions start around $43,468 annually, with experienced professionals earning $63,920+ per year. Senior payroll roles can exceed $76,093 annually. The field provides stable employment and clear advancement opportunities. Can I be a payroll specialist without a degree? Yes, many successful payroll professionals advance without college degrees. Experience and professional certifications like FPC or CPP often matter more than formal education. Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and payroll knowledge typically outweigh educational requirements. How long does it take to become a payroll assistant? Most people can qualify for entry-level payroll positions within 3-6 months of focused preparation. Employers typically provide comprehensive on-the-job training, so basic math and computer skills combined with willingness to learn often suffice for getting started. Do I need certification to be a payroll assistant? Certification isn’t required for entry-level positions, but earning credentials like FPC demonstrates commitment and improves job prospects. Many professionals pursue certification after gaining initial experience to advance their careers. Can payroll assistants work remotely? Yes, remote payroll opportunities are increasingly common since cloud-based software enables location-independent work. Many companies offer fully remote positions, and virtual payroll assistant services are growing as businesses embrace flexible work arrangements. Conclusion: Is payroll assistant the right career for you? If you’re detail-oriented, enjoy working with numbers, and want a stable career with clear advancement opportunities, becoming a payroll assistant could be your perfect entry point into finance and HR. The field offers competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and multiple paths for growth—from specialist roles to management positions. The best part? You don’t need years of education or experience to get started. With basic math skills, attention to detail, and willingness to learn, you can begin building a rewarding payroll career that provides job security and room to grow. {{banner-cta}}

title: AutoZone 1st Quarter Total Company Same Store Sales Increase 4.7%; Domestic Same Store Sales Increase 4.8%; 1st Quarter EPS of $31.04
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about AutoZone, Inc's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: AutoZone 1st Quarter Total Company Same Store Sales Increase 4.7%; Domestic Same Store Sales Increase 4.8%; 1st Quarter EPS of $31.04 Dec 09, 2025 PDF Version MEMPHIS, Tenn., Dec. 09, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AutoZone, Inc. (NYSE: AZO) today reported net sales of $4.6 billion for its first quarter (12 weeks) ended November 22, 2025, an increase of 8.2% from the first quarter of fiscal 2025 (12 weeks). Same store sales, or sales for our domestic and international stores open at least one year, are as follows: Constant Currency 12 Weeks 12 Weeks* Domestic 4.8 % 4.8 % International 11.2 % 3.7 % Total Company 5.5 % 4.7 % * Excludes impacts from fluctuations of foreign exchange rates. For the quarter, gross profit, as a percentage of sales, was 51.0%, a decrease of 203 basis points versus the prior year. The decrease in gross margin was driven by a 212 basis point non-cash LIFO impact, partially offset by other net margin improvements. Operating expenses, as a percentage of sales, were 34.0% versus last year at 33.3%. Deleverage was primarily driven by investments to support our growth initiatives. Operating profit decreased 6.8% to $784.2 million. Net income for the quarter was $530.8 million compared to $564.9 million in the same period last year, while diluted earnings per share were $31.04 compared to last year at $32.52. Under its share repurchase program, AutoZone repurchased 108 thousand shares of its common stock during the first quarter, at an average price per share of $3,999, for a total investment of $431.1 million. At the end of the first quarter, the Company had $1.7 billion remaining under its current share repurchase authorization. The Company’s inventory increased 13.9% over the same period last year, driven primarily by growth initiatives and inflation. Net inventory, defined as merchandise inventories less accounts payable, on a per store basis, was negative $145 thousand versus negative $166 thousand last year and negative $131 thousand last quarter. “I would like to thank our AutoZoners for delivering another quarter of strong sales growth. Our Domestic and International businesses performed well throughout the quarter as we continue to execute on our growth initiatives. We were especially pleased to open 53 net new stores globally in the quarter and we plan to aggressively open stores over the remainder of the fiscal year as we continue our focus on gaining market share. As we invest in growing our business, we will remain committed to our disciplined approach of increasing earnings and cash flow to drive shareholder value,” said Phil Daniele, President and Chief Executive Officer. During the quarter ended November 22, 2025, AutoZone opened 39 new stores in the U.S., 12 in Mexico and two in Brazil for a total of 53 net new stores. As of November 22, 2025, the Company had 6,666 stores in the U.S., 895 in Mexico and 149 in Brazil for a total store count of 7,710. AutoZone is a leading retailer and distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories in the Americas. Each store carries an extensive product line for cars, sport utility vehicles, vans and light duty trucks, including new and remanufactured automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories, and non-automotive products. The majority of stores have a commercial sales program that provides prompt delivery of parts and other products and commercial credit to local, regional and national repair garages, dealers, service stations, fleet owners and other accounts. AutoZone also sells automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories and non-automotive products through www.autozone.com , and our commercial customers can make purchases through www.autozonepro.com . Additionally, we sell the ALLDATA brand of automotive diagnostic, repair, collision and shop management software through www.alldata.com . We also provide product information on our Duralast branded products through www.duralastparts.com . AutoZone does not derive revenue from automotive repair or installation services. AutoZone will host a conference call this morning, Tuesday, December 9, 2025, beginning at 10:00 a.m. (ET) to discuss its first quarter results. This call is being web cast and can be accessed, along with supporting slides, at AutoZone’s website at www.autozone.com by clicking on Investor Relations. Investors may also listen to the call by dialing (888) 506-0062, passcode AUTOZONE. In addition, a telephone replay will be available by dialing (877) 481-4010, replay passcode 52975 through December 23, 2025. title: BCP Investment Corporation Announces Final Results of Its Modified “Dutch Auction” Tender Offer
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about BCP Investment Corporation's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version Shares Tendered at $13.63 Per Share, Generating NAV Accretion of Approximately 1.0%¹ NEW YORK, Dec. 12, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BCP Investment Corporation (NASDAQ: BCIC) (“BCIC” or the “Company”) today announced the final results of its modified “Dutch Auction” tender offer (the “Offer”) to purchase for cash up to an aggregate of $9.0 million in value of shares of its common stock, par value $0.01 per share, which expired at 11:59 P.M. ET on December 10, 2025. Based on the final count by Broadridge Corporate Issuer Solutions LLC, the depositary and paying agent for the Offer (the “Depositary”), a total of 4.4 million shares of BCIC’s common stock were validly tendered and not properly withdrawn at or below the purchase price of $14.93 per share, including shares that were tendered through notice of guaranteed delivery. The Offer was made by a group consisting of (i) BCP Investment Corporation, (ii) Edward Goldthorpe, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, (iii) Patrick Schafer, Chief Investment Officer of the Company, (iv) Brandon Satoren, Chief Financial Officer of the Company, (v) Joseph Morea, a member of the Company’s Board of Directors, (vi) George Grunebaum, a member of the Company’s Board of Directors, (vii) Sam Reinhart, an officer at an entity affiliated with the Company’s investment adviser, and (viii) Nikita Klassen, an officer at an entity affiliated with the Company’s investment adviser (collectively, with the Company, the “Offeror Group”). Each member of the Offeror Group purchased shares, severally and not jointly. In accordance with the terms and conditions of the Offer, the Offeror Group has accepted for purchase a total of 0.7 million shares of its common stock at a purchase price of $13.63 per share, for an aggregate cost of approximately $9.0 million excluding fees and expenses relating to the Offer. The 0.7 million shares accepted for purchase in the Offer represent approximately 5% of BCIC’s outstanding shares as of December 12, 2025. The Company purchased approximately the first $7.6 million of tendered shares, and the other members of the Offeror Group purchased, severally, and not jointly, approximately the remaining $1.4 million of tendered shares. The Depositary will promptly pay for the shares accepted for purchase in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Offer. Questions regarding the tender offer may be directed to Broadridge Corporate Issuer Solutions, LLC at (855) 793-5068. About BCP Investment Corporation BCP Investment Corporation (Nasdaq: BCIC) is a publicly traded, externally managed closed-end investment company that has elected to be regulated as a business development company under the Investment Company Act of 1940. BCIC’s middle market investment business originates, structures, finances and manages a portfolio of term loans, mezzanine investments and selected equity securities in middle market companies. BCIC’s investment activities are managed by its investment adviser, Sierra Crest Investment Management LLC, an affiliate of BC Partners Advisors L.P. BCIC’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, earnings releases, press releases and other financial, operational and governance information are available on BCIC’s website at www.bcpinvestmentcorporation.com . title: How AI Personalization Improves Knowledge Base Search Results - Ariglad
summary: AI-powered personalization transforms knowledge base search from a generic lookup tool into an intelligent assistant that understands your users' unique contexts and delivers precisely the answers they need.
body_text: We've all been there. You're frantically searching your company's knowledge base for an answer, typing in what feels like the perfect query, and getting back... a wall of vaguely related articles that don't quite hit the mark. You click through three, four, maybe five articles before finding what you need—if you find it at all. It's frustrating for users, and it's expensive for support teams. Every failed search is a potential ticket, a frustrated customer, and another drain on your agents' time. But here's the thing: your knowledge base probably has the answer. The problem isn't what you've documented—it's how users find it. That's where AI personalization comes in. What Makes Traditional Knowledge Base Search Fall Short? Traditional knowledge base search works like a slightly smarter version of Ctrl+F. You type in keywords, and it surfaces articles containing those exact words or close variations. The problem? This approach treats every user the same. A brand-new customer searching for "setup" gets the same results as a power user searching for the same term. Someone on the Basic plan sees the same articles as someone on Enterprise. A developer looking for API documentation gets mixed in with end-user how-tos. The result? Irrelevant results, wasted time, and a knowledge base that feels harder to navigate than it should be. How AI Personalization Changes the Game AI personalization doesn't just match keywords—it understands context. Modern AI can analyze who's searching, what they've searched before, what features they use, and even how they phrase their questions to deliver results that actually matter to them . Here's what that looks like in practice: Context-aware ranking : AI looks at the user's role, subscription level, and product usage to prioritize the most relevant articles. If you're an admin searching for "permissions," you'll see advanced configuration guides first. If you're a standard user, you'll see basic access instructions. Natural language understanding : Users don't need to guess the right keywords anymore. AI-powered semantic search understands intent, so "How do I get my team onboarded?" surfaces the same articles as "bulk user import" or "adding multiple users." Behavioral learning : The system gets smarter over time. If users consistently click the third result instead of the first, AI picks up on that pattern and adjusts future rankings accordingly. Dynamic content adaptation : Based on a user's account settings, feature access, or geographic location, AI can surface region-specific or plan-specific documentation automatically. Real Results: What Better Search Actually Delivers The impact of personalized search isn't just theoretical—it shows up in metrics that matter: Deflection rates improve as users find answers on their own instead of opening tickets Time to resolution drops when agents can quickly find the right internal documentation Self-service adoption increases when users trust that search will actually work Support costs decrease as fewer questions make it to your team Why Your Knowledge Base Needs More Than Just Better Search Here's the catch: personalized search only works if your knowledge base is actually accurate and up to date . The best AI in the world can't help users find information that's outdated, incomplete, or simply missing. This is where most teams hit a wall. Maintaining a knowledge base is tedious, time-consuming work. Articles drift out of sync with product updates. New features ship without documentation. Support agents keep answering the same questions because no one's had time to write the article yet. How Ariglad Keeps Your Knowledge Base Actually Useful This is exactly the problem Ariglad was built to solve. Ariglad delivers a powerful set of tools built to keep your knowledge base accurate and up to date. It intelligently reviews support tickets, detects missing or outdated information, and refreshes your documentation automatically. With AI woven into your support operations, Ariglad helps your team resolve issues faster, lighten the load on agents, and maintain a knowledge base that grows alongside your business. Here's how it works in practice: Automated gap detection : Ariglad analyzes your support tickets to identify patterns—questions that keep coming up that don't have corresponding articles, instead of manually combing through tickets to figure out what's missing. Smart content suggestions : When Ariglad spots missing or outdated content, it doesn't just flag the problem—it drafts new articles or updates based on actual support interactions. Your team reviews and approves, but the heavy lifting is done. Continuous monitoring : Products change. Features evolve. Ariglad continuously monitors your tickets and product updates to catch when existing articles need refreshing, ensuring your knowledge management system stays current without manual audits. Intelligent search optimization : Ariglad helps ensure that users searching your knowledge base find the most relevant, accurate information—because the content itself is actively maintained and improved based on real usage patterns. The result? A knowledge base that actually serves its purpose: giving users answers when they need them, reducing ticket volume , and freeing up your support team to handle complex issues that genuinely need human expertise. The Bottom Line AI personalization makes knowledge base search dramatically better—but only when paired with content that's worth finding. Generic, outdated, or incomplete documentation won't cut it, no matter how smart your search algorithm is. The winning combination is intelligent search that understands your users and intelligent content management that keeps your knowledge base accurate and comprehensive. That's how you turn your knowledge base from a neglected repository into a genuine support asset. When users can trust that searching will get them real answers—fast—they'll stop flooding your inbox with questions. Your support team can focus on genuinely complex problems. And your knowledge base becomes what it was always meant to be: your first line of support, not your last resort. Ready to see what AI-powered knowledge management can do for your team? That's what Ariglad is here for. ‍ Book a Demo With Ariglad
